chapter: New York: 52nd Street and Lester Young
title: Prez's decline and Stan Getz
summary: Prez's drinking cost him his appetite; younger saxophonists like Stan Getz hung around his room.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: But -- and that kind of helped him to kind of pull out of it for a while. But then he started getting back on

the bottle and drank so much that he lost his taste for food, you know, and that's what actually carried him to his deterioration. In the meantime Stan Getz and all those guys would go around to his room every night and -- sometime he'd tell me, man, I say I'm going home. He said, man, he said, 'Stay here.' Maybe we can get these guys to leave, you know. They come around to his room every night to sit around and listen to his old records and have him explain to them, you know, just hung right on him, you know.
And they won an award, and he never won an award.
He -- did he -- did he resent the people like Getz who were --
No. No, he kind of liked it, because everybody knew that was him.
Yeah, well, that's the proper way to look at it, although, of course, they -- the --
